property_summary: Invariant: after a user deposits X and then calls withdrawAll, the user's credit is always reset to 0; the buggy mutant resets credit before the external call which can cause a reentrant attacker to withdraw more than their balance (the reference's reentrancy lock prevents reentrant double-withdrawal).

For any depositor and any deposit amount, if a malicious reentrant callee attempts to reenter during withdrawAll, the reference contract (with reentrancy lock) ensures the depositor's funds cannot be withdrawn twice (address(c).balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount and withdraw completes without reentrant extra draining), whereas the mutant that zeroes credit before the external call allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw more than intended causing address(c).balance to drop further (the property: after withdrawAll by attacker, address(c).balance == initialBalance - withdrawnAmount for all inputs; the mutant can violate this).

For any depositor and any deposit amount, after deposit() and a subsequent withdrawAll() initiated by that depositor, the contract's balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount (no extra loss); the mutant allowing reentrancy can cause a deeper drain so this equality can be violated for some inputs involving a reentrant attacker helper.

For any attacker-deposit amount and attacker address, if the attacker deposits some ether and then calls withdrawAll via a contract that reenters during the external call, the reference contract's reentrancy lock ensures the withdraw call returns normally (no nested withdraw succeeds) so address(c).balance == initialBalance - withdrawnAmount after the call; the mutant allowing credit to be zeroed before the external call enables a reentrant nested withdraw to succeed and can make address(c).balance drop below that expected value (so the property is violated).

For any depositor address and deposit amount, if a benign recipient contract that REVERTS on receive is used as the msg.sender when calling withdrawAll, the reference C will revert the withdraw (so the call fails and c.balance remains unchanged) while the mutant that zeroes credit before the external call will still revert but the timing of state changes differs — therefore the general rule: when an external call from withdrawAll to the recipient reverts, the reference contract leaves c.balance unchanged and the call overall reverts (so try/catch reports failure); the mutant can allow state changes to persist across the failing external call and thus can make the external call outcome differ — the test detects the difference by asserting that withdrawAll always reverts (ok == false) for a reverter callee after a deposit.

After a successful withdrawAll by a caller, the contract's recorded credit for that caller is zero in the reference implementation for every input; the mutant that performs the external call before clearing credit allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw twice and thus leaves a nonzero observed balance difference (or enables double-withdrawal), violating the invariant.

For any caller and deposit amount, after withdrawAll returns the contract's recorded credit for that caller is zero (and address(c).balance decreased by that amount); the mutant that calls the external transfer before clearing credit allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw twice, breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after calling withdrawAll the contract's recorded credit for that depositor becomes zero (and address(c).balance has decreased by exactly that amount) in the reference; the mutant that performs the external call before zeroing credit enables a reentrant attacker to withdraw twice, breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For any attacker address and deposit amount, if the attacker deposits X and then calls withdrawAll, the reference contract never allows the attacker to receive more than X (so address(c).balance decreases by exactly X and the withdraw call succeeds exactly once); the mutant that performs the external call before clearing state can be reentered and thus allows the attacker to extract more than X, violating the invariant.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after the depositor calls withdrawAll the contract's stored credit for that depositor is zero (and address(c).balance decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount); the mutant that does the external call before clearing state allows a reentrant attacker to call back and withdraw more than its credit, violating this invariant for some inputs.

After a depositor calls withdrawAll, the depositor's recorded credit is always zero in the correct contract (reentrancy-locked), but removing the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker to observe non-zero credit after withdrawAll (so the invariant credit[caller]==0 after withdrawAll can be violated by the mutant).

For any depositor and deposit amount, after calling withdrawAll the contract's recorded credit for that depositor is zero in the reference (reentrancy lock prevents double-withdraw), but removing the lock allows a reentrant attacker to reenter withdrawAll and observe non-zero credit, so the invariant credit[caller] == 0 after withdrawAll holds for the reference for all inputs and is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after a successful withdrawAll call the contract's balance equals prior balance minus the withdrawn amount (i.e., withdrawals drain stored balance atomically); removing the reentrancy lock can allow reentrant double-withdraw causing address(c).balance to be lower than expected, violating this invariant for some inputs.

Rule: For any depositor and deposit amount, a non-reverting external callee used as the recipient of withdrawAll will always receive exactly the deposited amount in the reference (no double-send), but the mutant without the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker recipient to cause more than the deposited amount to be sent (double-withdraw) for some inputs.

For any depositor address and deposit amount, a malicious recipient that reenters via receive() cannot cause withdrawAll to send Ether twice: in the correct contract the recipient's reentrant call cannot increase the total Ether sent out (address(c).balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount), whereas removing the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker to double-withdraw and make address(c).balance decrease by more than the single withdrawal for some inputs.
